annotation.evidence_span: An application MUST be able to set the value for R2
annotation.interpretation_a: The application has direct control over the R2 value, and can modify it at any time during the connection's lifetime.
annotation.interpretation_b: The application can *influence* the R2 value, perhaps by providing a suggestion or preference, but the system may ultimately decide the final value based on other factors.
annotation.justification: The phrase "able to set" is vague. It doesn't specify if the application's setting is guaranteed to be used, or if there are any limitations on when or how the setting can be applied. This creates ambiguity about the actual implementation behavior.
annotation.missing_information: The clause does not specify *how* the application sets R2, or whether the setting is a one-time configuration or can be changed dynamically. It also doesn't specify if the setting is honored by the TCP implementation.
